from: October book, night 28 (A Fire in My Bones)
p1: The Lord sent Jeremiah to stand at the gate of His house, the temple. Jeremiah gave the people the Lord’s words. “Obey My voice, and you will be My people.”
Many people did not want to listen. Some laughed at Jeremiah every day. One leader even locked him up for a night.
Jeremiah felt sad. He thought, “I will not speak about the Lord anymore.”
p2: But Jeremiah said the Lord’s word was in his heart. It was “like a burning fire shut up in my bones.” It was a warm, strong feeling he could not hold in. So Jeremiah kept on sharing.
Jesus’s words can feel warm in your heart too. Tonight, tell your family one thing you love about Him.
old: Long ago there was a city called Jerusalem. A man named Jeremiah lived there. Heavenly Father gave Jeremiah words to say to the people. Someone who shares Heavenly Father's words is called a prophet.

The people had stopped listening to Heavenly Father. Jeremiah's job was to say, "Come back to Him. He loves you." But the people did not want to hear it. Some of them were unkind to Jeremiah. Some days he felt tired and sad. He thought, "Maybe I will just stay quiet."

But the words would not stay quiet. Jeremiah said they felt like a little fire burning inside him. He picked fire for a picture because fire is warm, and fire wiggles and moves, and you cannot hide a fire under your coat. Jeremiah tried and tried to hold the words in. He could not.

So Jeremiah opened his mouth, and out came a song. "Sing to the Lord! Praise the Lord!" he sang. The Lord is a name for Heavenly Father. To praise means to say out loud how good someone is. Even on a hard, tired day, the good thing inside Jeremiah came out as singing.

Heavenly Father put a warm little light inside you too. Tonight, before you close your eyes, let a little bit of it out. Tell one person one good thing about them. Or sing one quiet line of a song you love. A tired day cannot blow your light out.
